title: Argon Laser PRP: Pan-Retinal Photocoagulation
summary: A foundational ophthalmic intervention using Argon gas laser technology to treat ischemic retinal diseases. This procedure targets the peripheral retina to prevent severe vision loss from neovascularization.

sections.title: Primary Clinical Indications
content: Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion (BRVO) with Neovascularization

sections.title: The Mechanism of Action
content: Step 1: Argon laser creates thermal burns in the peripheral retina.
Step 2: Destruction of metabolic high-demand ischemic tissue.
Step 3: Reduction in Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) production.
Step 4: Regression of abnormal, fragile new blood vessels.

rows: Titrated to achieve a 'creamy white' burn

sections.title: Procedure Red Flags & Complications
content: Accidental Foveal Burn (Permanent central vision loss)

content.explanation: N: Night vision reduction; P: Peripheral visual field constriction; C: Color vision alterations.

sections.title: Verbatim Procedural Summary
sections.content: Argon laser PRP is performed to stabilize the retina by sacrificing peripheral vision to preserve central vision. The Argon laser's specific wavelength is highly absorbed by the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and hemoglobin, making it an effective tool for thermal photocoagulation in the treatment of proliferative vascular diseases.
